note: What a `safe` run of Claude Code may do that a folder's own settings allow, recorded on Claude Code 2.1.327 and the Agent SDK 0.3.332 on macOS, 2026-11-25, each run as this daemon builds it (`claudeArgs` for `claude -p`, `loadSdk` for the SDK) with a throwaway home. Folders are replaced by neutral ones, the prompt by a mark, and each result line's `credential_expires_at` (when the real sign-in expires) is left out; nothing else. Each run's folder holds `.claude/settings.json` = `settings` (else the top-level `settings`), the prompt asks for `touch allowed.txt` and `touch denied.txt` (and `touch user.txt` where the person's own settings allow it, `user_allow`), and `trusted` is the folder the config dir's `.claude.json` says the person trusted (`hasTrustDialogAccepted`), or null. `argv` is what Claude Code was started with (under the SDK, what the SDK gave it), `stderr` and `result` what it printed (its `result` line), `expect.ran` and `expect.denied` what happened on disk and in `permission_denials`, `expect.dropped` what a reader takes from stderr as Claude Code's reason for leaving the folder's allow rules out (`droppedRules`), and `expect.tail` what the daemon puts after the reply (`refusedNote`). `sdk-untrusted` has no recorded result line, only its argv and stderr: packages/cli/test/control-sdk.test.ts gives the SDK its stderr with `p-untrusted`'s result line, the same denials as Claude Code prints them on either path. The SDK runs were told `settingSources`; 0.3.332 reads all three by default (sdkReadsAllSettings), so the daemon tells it the same.
